changed.title: With one row and one column on, two ORs pairing four once-read inputs force equal crossed entries for gates of any kind reading earlier wires
changed.statement:
∀ (n m : ℕ) (G : Fin n → Fin m → Bool)
  (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit)
  (u u' : Fin n) (b b' : Fin m),
  let x := u.val
  let x' := u'.val
  let y := n + b.val
  let y' := n + b'.val
  let paired := fun (r c : ℕ) =>
    ∃ g ∈ C.gates, g.op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or ∧
      (g.inputs = [r, c] ∨ g.inputs = [c, r])
  u ≠ u' → b ≠ b' →
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (n + m) C →
  PEqualNP.Represents.Represents G C →
  paired x y → paired x' y' →
  (∀ w ∈ [x, x', y, y'],
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.readsIn C (Finset.range C.size) w = 1) →
  C.output ∉ [x, x', y, y'] →
  G u b' = G u' b
changed.unlocks: a tool for counting how often a line is read on the one-a-side promise, for the line of what a second read of a row costs; it moves no bound by itself
changed.context: On paper. Compare the two inputs (u, b') and (u', b). On both, the OR reading row u with column b and the OR reading row u' with column b' are true. Each of the four special input wires is read at one operand position only, the one in its OR, so no other gate reads any of them. Induct along the gate list: away from the four wires the two inputs give equal wire values; at the two ORs both values are true; at any other gate the operand values are equal, so its value is equal. The output wire is none of the four inputs, so the outputs agree. Represents turns them into G(u, b') and G(u', b).
changed.sketch: On paper. Compare the two inputs (u, b') and (u', b). On both, the OR reading row u with column b and the OR reading row u' with column b' are true. Each of the four special input wires is read at one operand position only, the one in its OR, so no other gate reads any of them. Induct along the gate list: away from the four wires the two inputs give equal wire values; at the two ORs both values are true; at any other gate the operand values are equal, so its value is equal. The output wire is none of the four inputs, so the outputs agree. Represents turns them into G(u, b') and G(u', b).

changed.title: On the one-a-side promise with AND/OR gates of fan-in exactly two, each edge in a nonfull row and column lights an AND whose operands split the two singletons
changed.statement:
∀ (n m : ℕ) (G : Fin n → Fin m → Bool) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit),
  PEqualNP.TopForm.IsAO2 (n + m) C →
  PEqualNP.Represents.Represents G C →
  ∀ (u : Fin n) (v : Fin m), G u v = true →
    (∃ c : Fin m, G u c = false) → (∃ r : Fin n, G r v = false) →
    let rowOnly := List.ofFn (fun r₀ : Fin n => decide (r₀ = u)) ++ List.replicate m false
    let colOnly := List.replicate n false ++ List.ofFn (fun c₀ : Fin m => decide (c₀ = v))
    let value := fun (x : List Bool) (w : ℕ) => (C.wires x).getD w false
    let split := fun (left right : ℕ) =>
      value rowOnly left = true ∧ value rowOnly right = false ∧
      value colOnly right = true ∧ value colOnly left = false
    ∃ (j : Fin C.gates.length) (a b : ℕ),
      (C.gates.get j).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and ∧
      (C.gates.get j).inputs = [a, b] ∧
      value (PEqualNP.Represents.oneEach u v) (n + m + j.val) = true ∧
      (split a b ∨ split b a)
changed.unlocks: the AND gate at which each edge comes to need both of its inputs in an AND/OR circuit on the one-a-side promise, a tool for the counts of that line; it moves no bound by itself
changed.context: On paper. Take three inputs: row u alone, column v alone, and the pair. The output is off on each single line, since a non-edge in that row or column would otherwise be on by monotonicity; it is on at the pair. Take the earliest wire that is on at the pair and off on both single lines. It is not an input. It is not an OR: an operand on at the pair is earlier, so a single line turns it on, and then the OR too. So it is an AND; both operands are on at the pair, each is turned on by a single line, and neither line turns on both. So the row alone lights one operand and the column alone the other.
changed.sketch: On paper. Take three inputs: row u alone, column v alone, and the pair. The output is off on each single line, since a non-edge in that row or column would otherwise be on by monotonicity; it is on at the pair. Take the earliest wire that is on at the pair and off on both single lines. It is not an input. It is not an OR: an operand on at the pair is earlier, so a single line turns it on, and then the OR too. So it is an AND; both operands are on at the pair, each is turned on by a single line, and neither line turns on both. So the row alone lights one operand and the column alone the other.

changed.title: Row containment through a dominating wire on the one-a-side promise for AND/OR gates of fan-in at most two reading earlier wires
changed.statement:
∀ (n m : ℕ) (G : Fin n → Fin m → Bool) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit)
    (u v : Fin n) (O : ℕ),
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C →
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (n + m) C →
  PEqualNP.Represents.Represents G C →
  u ≠ v →
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.readsIn C (Finset.range C.gates.length) u.val = 1 →
  C.output ≠ u.val →
  O < n + m + C.gates.length →
  (∀ c : Fin m, (C.wires (PEqualNP.Represents.oneEach v c)).getD O false = true) →
  (¬ Relation.TransGen
    (fun a b : ℕ => a ≠ O ∧ b ≠ O ∧
      ∃ j : Fin C.gates.length, b = n + m + j.val ∧
        a ∈ (PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.gateAt C j.val).inputs)
    u.val C.output) →
  ∀ c : Fin m, G u c = true → G v c = true
changed.unlocks: a tool for the count of names against literals on the one-a-side promise, used where every row is read once by an OR; it moves no bound by itself
changed.context: On paper. Fix a column c. Call a wire safe if every operand path to it from the input for row u passes through O, the empty path counted. O is on at (v, c). Every other safe input wire has value at (u, c) at most its value at (v, c). For a safe gate other than O all operands are safe, since a path avoiding O would extend to the gate. Induct along earlier wires: AND and OR are monotone, so each safe wire's value at (u, c) is at most its value at (v, c). The output is safe; apply this there and use that the circuit represents the graph. An absent output reads false.
changed.sketch: On paper. Fix a column c. Call a wire safe if every operand path to it from the input for row u passes through O, the empty path counted. O is on at (v, c). Every other safe input wire has value at (u, c) at most its value at (v, c). For a safe gate other than O all operands are safe, since a path avoiding O would extend to the gate. Induct along earlier wires: AND and OR are monotone, so each safe wire's value at (u, c) is at most its value at (v, c). The output is safe; apply this there and use that the circuit represents the graph. An absent output reads false.

changed.statement: ∃ (x1 : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (x2 : ℕ), x1.size ≤ (22 : ℕ) ∧ PEqualNP.TopForm.IsAO2 (14 : ℕ) x1 ∧ (∀ x3 ∈ x1.gates, x3.inputs.Nodup) ∧ x2 < (14 : ℕ) + x1.size ∧ x2 ≠ (2 : ℕ) ∧ ∀ (x3 : Fin (14 : ℕ) → Bool), PEqualNP.BlindGate.wireValue x1 (14 : ℕ) x3 x2 = Bool.true ↔ ∃ (x4 : Fin (7 : ℕ)) (x5 : Fin (7 : ℕ)), x4 ≠ (2 : Fin (7 : ℕ)) ∧ (x4 = x5 ∨ x4 = x5 + (1 : Fin (7 : ℕ)) ∨ x4 = x5 + (3 : Fin (7 : ℕ))) ∧ x3 (Fin.castAdd (7 : ℕ) x4) = Bool.true ∧ x3 (Fin.natAdd (7 : ℕ) x5) = Bool.true

changed.title: The two-lit function of the graph H on 6 points with mask 274910127 on shared wires has an AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in two with at most 6 gates
changed.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 6 ∧ ∀ i j : Fin 6, C.eval (List.ofFn fun k : Fin 6 => decide (k = i ∨ k = j)) = (274910127 : ℕ).testBit (6 * min i.val j.val + max i.val j.val)
changed.unlocks: the exact size of the two-lit-points function of this graph on six shared wires; the family shows where a NOT gate pays with no equal lines
changed.sketch: We hold a circuit of 7 gates, a weak hand form (best over a few point orders and the complement plus a NOT, equal gates merged): OR(0,1), OR(2,6), NOT(7), AND(5,8), AND(4,7), OR(9,10), NOT(11) (inputs 0-5 are the points, gate k is wire 6 + k, output last). We hold no circuit of 6 gates; this is a search. No complete search of ours has run at six points.
